financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (Bank standalone) basis. EPS 14.18 = 16,628,598k/1,172,700,760 confirmed exactly. See GROUP row's notes for shared extraction/verification detail.

Sampath Bank PLC, a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). This filing reports on a 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE basis (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) rather than a discrete quarter -- the filing itself leads with these H1 figures in its financial commentary (and also separately provides quarter-only columns, which were not used for consistency with prior single-quarter entries; this entry is the H1 cumulative figure). Mapped per this project's bank/NBFI convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (Net interest income + Net fee & commission income + Net gain from trading + Net gain on derecognition of financial assets + Net other operating income); operating_profit = 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services', the Bank's own subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- Interest expense is already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income, so a separate line would double count. 'Total taxes on financial services' (VAT + Social Security Contribution Levy, Rs.7,354,895k Bank / Rs.7,966,805k Group for H1 2026) is not a separate stored field -- profit_before_tax stored here is AFTER this levy, matching the filing's own 'Profit before income tax' line. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split, and 'Financial assets at amortised cost - loans & advances' is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks'. long_term_borrowings = 'due to other borrowers' + 'due to debt securities holders' (debentures). 'Due to depositors' (Rs.1,741,279,931k Bank / Rs.1,781,513,079k Group) is deliberately excluded from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt. EPS cross-check: Bank 16,628,598k/1,172,700,760 shares=14.18 exact match to disclosed 14.18; Group 17,859,576k/1,172,700,760=15.23 exact match to disclosed 15.23 -- both tie precisely, no column-swap issues (this filing's tables were consistently ordered throughout, unlike some others processed this session). capex (Bank) = 'Purchase of property, plant & equipment' (2,242,929) + 'Purchase of intangible assets' (923,961) = 3,166,890; capex (Group) = 2,610,883+969,406=3,580,289.

interim_updates.note_text: Sampath Bank Group's Total Operating Income grew 17.4% YoY to Rs.68.13bn for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026; Bank-only: Rs.63.25bn, +16.5%), driven by Net Interest Income +12.4% (Rs.41.32bn to Rs.46.43bn) and Net Fee & Commission Income +26.1% (Rs.10.19bn to Rs.12.84bn). By segment (Group), growth was led by SME & Retail Banking, whose segment result rose 18.1% YoY (Rs.19.83bn to Rs.23.41bn) -- the largest single contributor -- while Dealing/Investment segment result FELL 34.8% (Rs.15.30bn to Rs.9.98bn), explained by the filing's own commentary: capital gains from Treasury bill/bond sales moderated to Rs.1.0bn from Rs.3.5bn in the comparative period, as fewer opportunities for gains arose in the prevailing market. Corporate Banking grew a more modest 6.1% (Rs.9.85bn to Rs.10.45bn). The Bank's earnings were also moderated by a sharply higher impairment charge: Rs.4.96bn for H1 2026 vs just Rs.1.17bn in H1 2025 (+324%), driven by collective impairment on an 18% expansion of the loan portfolio (vs 7% growth in H1 2025) and additional management-overlay provisioning for geopolitical uncertainty, per the filing's own explanation. Operating expenses grew 21.4% (Rs.21.72bn to Rs.26.37bn) on workforce expansion, salary revisions and technology investment, pushing the Cost-to-Income Ratio to 41.7% from 40.0%. Despite these headwinds, Bank Profit After Tax still grew 13.2% YoY to Rs.16.63bn, helped by an 18% YoY fall in the income tax charge (finalisation of prior-year tax assessments). Net Interest Margin improved to 4.21% from 4.11%. Per the filing's own commentary (not separately verified here since no prior-quarter row exists in this database yet), the Bank's Q2 2026 profit rose 69% quarter-on-quarter, driven by a >Rs.3bn impairment reversal from recovered written-off loans.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for SAMP -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1) figures rather than a discrete quarter, since Sampath Bank has a 31 December FYE and reports this way; the filing's own quarter-only columns (also available) were not used, to keep this entry's period type consistent and unambiguous. The filing's own commentary states Bank PAT rose 69% quarter-on-quarter (Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026) on an impairment reversal exceeding Rs.3bn from recovered loans -- this QoQ figure is quoted from the filing's narrative only and has not been independently verified against stored quarter-level data, since none exists yet for this symbol.
interim_updates.takeaway: Core banking income growth (Total Operating Income +17%, Net Interest Margin expanding to 4.21%) is genuine and broad-based, led by SME & Retail Banking. The two things worth watching: (1) the sharp 324% YoY jump in the impairment charge, which the Bank attributes to loan growth and prudent geopolitical-risk provisioning rather than deteriorating asset quality (Stage 3 loans actually declined Rs.10.8bn), and (2) the Dealing/Investment segment's 35% profit decline, a normalisation of one-off Treasury gains rather than a core-business problem -- so PBT growth (+2.6%) understates the strength of core banking operations, which were partly offset by both of these largely non-recurring/prudential items.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Group Total Operating Income +17.4% YoY to Rs.68.13bn; Net Interest Income +12.4% to Rs.46.43bn; Net Fee & Commission Income +26.1% to Rs.12.84bn
SME & Retail Banking segment result +18.1% YoY (Rs.19.83bn to Rs.23.41bn) -- the largest driver of growth; Corporate Banking +6.1%
Dealing/Investment segment result -34.8% YoY (Rs.15.30bn to Rs.9.98bn) as capital gains from Treasury bill/bond sales moderated to Rs.1.0bn from Rs.3.5bn

Impairment charge +324% YoY to Rs.4.96bn (Bank), driven by 18% loan portfolio growth (vs 7% a year earlier) and additional management-overlay provisioning for geopolitical uncertainty; Stage 3 (impaired) loans actually declined Rs.10.8bn

Operating expenses +21.4% YoY, pushing Cost-to-Income Ratio to 41.7% from 40.0%; Bank PAT still grew 13.2% to Rs.16.63bn, helped by an 18% fall in the tax charge from prior-year tax assessment finalisation
Net Interest Margin improved to 4.21% from 4.11%; Return on Equity (after tax) rose to 18.91% from 17.93%; gross loan portfolio grew Rs.226bn (+18%) since year-end 2025
key_drivers: SME & Retail Banking segment (+18.1% YoY result, Rs.19.83bn to Rs.23.41bn) is the single largest driver of Group profit growth

Dealing/Investment segment result -34.8% YoY is the largest single drag, explicitly attributed by the Bank to a normalisation of Treasury bill/bond capital gains (Rs.3.5bn to Rs.1.0bn) rather than any operating weakness

The 324% YoY jump in impairment charges is a loan-growth-driven and prudential (management overlay for geopolitical risk) provisioning increase, not a sign of deteriorating asset quality -- Stage 3 loans fell Rs.10.8bn over the same period

Total Exchange Income rose 198% YoY to Rs.7.2bn (per the filing's commentary) on LKR depreciation against the USD, a meaningful contributor to non-fund-based income growth not separately broken out in the segmental table
